bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to motor vehicles; establishing Choose Life special license plates; appropriating money; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 168.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[168.1289] CHOOSE LIFE SPECIAL PLATES.

Subdivision 1.

Issuance of plates.

The commissioner must issue Choose Life special license plates or a single motorcycle plate to an applicant who:

(1) is a registered owner of a passenger automobile, noncommercial one-ton pickup truck, motorcycle, or recreational vehicle;

(2) pays special plate fees under section 168.12, subdivision 5, for each set of plates, along with any other fees required by this chapter;

(3) pays the registration tax as required under section 168.013;

(4) pays the fees required under this chapter;

(5) contributes $25 upon initial application and a minimum of $25 annually to the Choose Life account; and

(6) complies with this chapter and rules governing registration of motor vehicles and licensing of drivers.

Subd. 2.

Design.

The commissioner must adopt a suitable plate design that includes an image of the Choose Life kids logo in the design area on the left side of the plate and the inscription "Choose Life" on the bottom of the plate. A second suitable logo that includes an image of a silhouette of one adult and one child must be adopted by the commissioner by April 1, 2026.

Subd. 3.

Plates transfer.

On application to the commissioner and payment of a transfer fee of $5, special plates may be transferred to another qualified motor vehicle that is registered to the same individual to whom the special plates were originally issued.

Subd. 4.

Exemption.

Special plates issued under this section are not subject to section 168.1293, subdivision 2.

Subd. 5.

Contributions; account; appropriation.

Contributions collected under subdivision 1, clause (5), must be deposited in the Choose Life account, which is established in the special revenue fund. Money in the account is appropriated to the commissioner of public safety. This appropriation is first for the annual cost of administering the account funds, and the remaining funds are for distribution to Choose Life Minnesota, Inc., to be distributed to agencies as required under subdivision 6. The commissioner must include with its distribution to Choose Life Minnesota, Inc., a report specifying the ratio of contributions collected under subdivision 1, clause (5), in each county to the total contributions collected in the state.

Subd. 6.

Contribution recipient requirements.

(a) Using the county contribution report from the commissioner in subdivision 5, Choose Life Minnesota, Inc., must distribute each county's share of collected contributions to nongovernmental, nonprofit agencies within each county that assist pregnant women who are making adoption plans for their children. Funds may not be distributed to any agency that is involved in or associated with abortion activities, including counseling for or referrals to abortion clinics, providing medical abortion-related procedures, or pro-abortion advertising. Funds may not be distributed to any agency that charges women for services received.

(b) Agencies that receive funds under this subdivision must use the funds to provide for the material needs of pregnant women who are making adoption plans for their children, including but not limited to clothing, housing, medical care, food, utilities, and transportation. Agencies that receive funds under this subdivision may not provide or assist a woman to obtain adoption services from a provider that is not licensed. Funds may be expended to support birth mothers for 60 days after delivery and infants awaiting placement with adoptive parents and any adoption-related counseling, training, or advertising.

(c) Funds distributed under this section must not be used for administrative expenses, legal expenses, or capital expenditures except that Choose Life Minnesota, Inc., may use up to 15 percent of funds for administration and promotion of the Choose Life special license plate program.

(d) If no qualified agency applies to receive funds in a county in any year, that county's share of contributions collected under subdivision 1, clause (5), must be distributed proportionally to any qualified agencies that apply to receive funds and that maintain a place of business within a 150-mile radius of the county seat of the county containing no qualified agency. If no qualified agencies apply, the funds must be held by Choose Life Minnesota, Inc., until a qualified agency under this subdivision applies for the funds.

(e) Each agency that receives funds under this subdivision must submit an annual attestation to Choose Life Minnesota, Inc. Any unused funds that exceed ten percent of the funds received by an agency each year must be returned to Choose Life Minnesota, Inc., which must distribute the funds to other qualified agencies within the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective January 1, 2026, for special plates issued on or after that date.
